points.quote: The University does not ban you from using Gen-AI in your studies.  However, your use needs to be ethical and appropriate.
points.gist: Gen-AI is not banned, but use must be ethical and appropriate.

points.quote: The University has Gen-AI categories for assessment, which guide you on how Gen-AI can be used in completing the assessment.
points.gist: Assessment Gen-AI categories guide how Gen-AI can be used in completing an assessment.

points.quote: Gen-AI may be used to prepare for the assessment, however the type and logistics of the assessment mean it is not possible for you to be able to use Gen-AI software during the assessment itself.
points.gist: Category 1: Gen-AI may be used to prepare, but the assessment's type and logistics mean it cannot be used during it.

points.quote: You may use Gen-AI to help you complete the assessment, but must adhere to the guiding principle below and declare if and how you have used it using the Gen-AI coversheet.
points.gist: Category 2: Gen-AI may be used to help complete the assessment, following the guiding principle and declaring use on the coversheet.

points.quote: the fundamental content of the submission (e.g., the basic written expression, arguments, interpretations, conclusions etc.) of the work submitted should be your own.
points.gist: In Category 2 the fundamental content of the submission, such as basic written expression, arguments and conclusions, should be the student's own.

points.quote: These are designed so that you must use Gen-AI as part of the assessment requirements so as to support Gen-AI skills development.
points.gist: Category 3 assessments are designed so that Gen-AI must be used, to support Gen-AI skills development.

points.quote: You will complete and submit this with all Category 2 and Category 3 assessments.
points.gist: The Gen-AI coversheet is completed and submitted with all Category 2 and Category 3 assessments.

points.quote: it is possible that inappropriate or unethical use may contravene the University’s Academic Integrity Procedure and may be penalised as a result. For example, due to an instance of plagiarism or use of an essay mill or through breaching requirements for honesty (e.g. making a false declaration on the Gen-AI coversheet).
points.gist: Inappropriate or unethical use may breach the Academic Integrity Procedure and be penalised, for example through plagiarism, essay mill use or a false coversheet declaration.

points.quote: use of Gen-AI beyond that declared on the Gen-AI coversheet and/or misrepresentation of use, may represent a breach of the fitness to practice requirements for that programme.
points.gist: On programmes under the Fitness to Practise Procedure, use beyond what was declared or misrepresentation may breach fitness to practise requirements.

points.quote: Note: for Category 2 assessments, the basic written expression must be your own. So whilst Gen-AI may correct mistakes it must not produce the actual content.
points.gist: In Category 2, basic written expression must be the student's own; Gen-AI may correct mistakes but must not produce the actual content.

points.quote: If there are any subject-specific rules or requirements around Gen-AI that are set by professional or accrediting organizations, these will be communicated to you where necessary.
points.gist: Subject-specific rules set by professional or accrediting bodies will be communicated where necessary.

points.quote: If you do have any queries about a particular assessment, you should discuss this with the member of staff who set the assessment.
points.anchor: What if I have a question about an assessment?
points.gist: Discuss queries about a particular assessment with the staff member who set it.

points.quote: There is the potential for references to be fabricated.
points.anchor: What are the potential limitations of Gen-AI?
points.gist: There is potential for references to be fabricated.
